title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Financial Reasoning: A CFA-Based Benchmark Study
extended_summary:
This paper evaluates how well recent large language models can answer domain-specific multiple-choice questions drawn from official CFA mock exams. The central problem is whether state-of-the-art LLMs can perform the kind of long-context, quantitative, and conceptually integrated reasoning required for professional financial certification, and whether retrieval augmentation can improve performance over zero-shot prompting.

The study compares GPT-4o, GPT-o1, and o3-mini on 1,560 CFA mock questions spanning Levels I–III, using two approaches: zero-shot answering and a domain-reasoning Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. The RAG system retrieves relevant passages from the official CFA curriculum using generated summaries and keywords, then supplies the retrieved context to the model for answering. The paper also analyzes error types, readability, and question types (conceptual vs. calculation).

The population is not a human learner sample but the set of CFA exam questions, which represent adult professional financial certification content. The context is professional finance rather than schooling, and the task is benchmarking model performance on authentic exam materials. The main conclusion is that GPT-o1 performs best overall, RAG generally improves accuracy especially on more complex levels and knowledge-intensive topics, and most failures are due to missing domain knowledge rather than readability or simple arithmetic alone.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language models used for question answering, reasoning, and retrieval-augmented generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Benchmarked as zero-shot and RAG-enhanced models on CFA multiple-choice exam questions; the paper evaluates GPT-4o, GPT-o1, and o3-mini under the normalized ChatGPT family.

findings.finding_summary: Across 1,560 CFA mock questions, ChatGPT-family models showed strong financial reasoning performance, with GPT-o1 achieving the highest zero-shot accuracies at 94.78% (Level I), 89.32% (Level II), and 79.09% (Level III). RAG further improved performance at higher levels, with GPT-o1 rising to 91.36% on Level II and 87.73% on Level III.
findings.measure: Accuracy on CFA mock exam multiple-choice questions

findings.finding_summary: RAG improved performance most at higher difficulty levels, especially for GPT-o1 (+2.05 percentage points at Level II and +8.64 at Level III) and o3-mini (+4.55 at Level II and +5.45 at Level III). The paper reports minimal RAG gains at Level I, suggesting retrieval was more useful for complex, context-heavy questions.
findings.measure: Accuracy improvement from zero-shot to RAG across CFA levels

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark study of LLM performance on CFA exam questions, not a K-12 instructional intervention, and it does not evaluate a student-facing educational tool. The paper is empirical, but its relevance to the requested K-12 literacy topic is indirect.
impact_tier_rationale: No K-12 reading/literacy outcome is measured, and no direct student impact is reported. The findings concern finance-domain exam accuracy rather than educational effectiveness in elementary literacy instruction.
